domain_1:
    action in domain_1: (:action sell_cow_for_beans :parameters (?b ?cow ?j - entity ?beans - item ?l - location) :precondition (and (at ?j ?l) (at ?cow ?l) (offers ?b ?beans) (at ?b ?l)) :effect (and (has ?j ?beans) (not (offers ?b ?beans)) (not (at_item ?beans ?l))))
    predicates explaination in domain_1: {'(at ?e - entity ?l - location)': "relation 'at' holds; arguments: ?e is a entity, ?l is a location; used as precondition of sell_cow_for_beans, precondition of climb_beanstalk, effect of climb_beanstalk, precondition of ask_giant_wife_for_breakfast, precondition of hide_in_kettle, effect of hide_in_kettle, precondition of return_down_beanstalk, effect of return_down_beanstalk", '(at_item ?i - item ?l - location)': "relation 'at item' holds; arguments: ?i is a item, ?l is a location; used as effect of sell_cow_for_beans, precondition of plant_beans, effect of plant_beans, precondition of steal_gold_bags, effect of steal_gold_bags", '(has ?e - entity ?i - item)': "relation 'has' holds; arguments: ?e is a entity, ?i is a item; used as effect of sell_cow_for_beans, effect of steal_gold_bags, effect of steal_hen, effect of steal_harp", '(offers ?e - entity ?i - item)': "relation 'offers' holds; arguments: ?e is a entity, ?i is a item; used as precondition of sell_cow_for_beans, effect of sell_cow_for_beans"}

domain_2:
    action in domain_2: (:action donkey_kick_messenger :parameters (?donkey ?messenger - entity) :precondition (attempt_light ?messenger) :effect (kick ?donkey ?messenger))
    predicates explaination in domain_2: {'(attempt_light ?messenger - entity)': "entity ?messenger is in the state 'attempt light'; used as effect of messenger_attempt_light, precondition of cat_attack_messenger, precondition of dog_bite_messenger, precondition of donkey_kick_messenger", '(kick ?donkey - entity ?target - entity)': "relation 'kick' holds; arguments: ?donkey is a entity, ?target is a entity; used as effect of donkey_kick_messenger"}

Please judge whether the two operators can be merged into one action based on following rules:
(1) If the two actions have the same name, they MUST be merged into one action;
(2) If the two actions are semantically equivalent (although they may differ in preconditions and effects), merge them. Genrally, you need to union their preconditions and effects.
(3) Note that do NOT merge two actions if the logic becomes more complex after merging. For example, do NOT use "or", "when" to union two actions (about their preconditions and effects). Namely NOT too general. 
(4) Do NOT invent any predicate.
(5) If you decide to merge two actions. You can invent new action name. But the new name must be reasonable according to the whole predicates in the action.
    For example: if the action expresses the meaning of "pick some object from drawer" according to the predicates in preconditions and effects, just name it like "pick_from_drawer", instead of "pick_from_container", etc.
(6) Keep the given PDDL style. Please use PDDL 1.0 and do NOT use Conditional Effects like "when", etc.
(7) Note the number of brackets in the PDDL format.

Your output should include four part:
(1) reasoning: your analysis process;
(2) merge_flag: whether the two operators can be merged into one;
(3) new_operator_name: if equivalent, output the new operator name (in one of the given operator or a new invented operator).
(4) new_operator: if equivalent, output the new operator in PDDL format.

If "merge_flag" is false, the "new_operator_name" and "new_operator" parts are null.

Your output should be in JSON format like below:
{
    "reasoning": "your analysis process",
    "merge_flag": true,
    "new_operator_name": "open_door",
    "new_operator": "(:action open_door \n :parameters (?r ?d) \n :precondition (and (hand_free ?r)) \n :effect (and (is_open ?d)))"
}

Do NOT output any strange symbols like "\".
